title: Same Query, Different Answer: Run-to-Run Variance in Semantic Query Processing
summary: Semantic query engines ask a large language model (LLM) to judge individual rows, and benchmarks compare these engines on the quality of a few executions at temperature 0. We measure how much another execution changes. We re-execute the text and tabular workloads of SemBench, LRO-Bench, and UDA-Bench through their own harnesses, log every one of 1.2 million model calls, and reanalyze SemBench's published executions.
body: Semantic query engines ask a large language model (LLM) to judge individual rows, and benchmarks compare these engines on the quality of a few executions at temperature 0. We measure how much another execution changes. We re-execute the text and tabular workloads of SemBench, LRO-Bench, and UDA-Bench through their own harnesses, log every one of 1.2 million model calls, and reanalyze SemBench's published executions. At temperature 0, between 0.07% and 10.2% of rows change their operator output over five executions, depending on the model, and up to 24.0% on one task. Plans amplify these changes exponentially in the number of rows an answer exposes, as a possible-worlds model predicts: on UDA-Bench, a few percent of extracted values change, but about two thirds of the answers do. In SemBench's published results, 21% of text results change quality between executions, including on engines whose plans are deterministic. Several per-query system comparisons, and 16 of 28 tests of LRO-Bench's implementation recommendations, are not settled by the executions the benchmarks run. Changing rows are rows on which models disagree with each other; identical requests within one execution disagree as often as across executions; and one execution's decision margin or reasoning length predicts which rows change. Voting reduces the variance but does not remove it, and a calibrated cascade keeps its guarantee while the rows it returns change. We derive reporting rules for benchmarks and design rules for engines.
summaryZh: 本文研究了语义查询引擎在多次执行大语言模型调用时的运行间方差（Run-to-Run Variance）。通过重新执行多个主流基准测试并记录超过120万次模型调用，研究发现即便在温度为0的设置下，仍有相当比例的行输出和最终答案在不同执行间发生变化，计划执行会按行数呈指数级放大这种变化。文章最后为基准测试报告和引擎设计推导出了新的规则与建议。

aiReview.reasonZh: 该研究揭示了语义查询引擎在零温度下运行大语言模型时存在的显著运行间方差，对大模型基准测试评测方法具有重要的实践指导意义。

glossary.explanationZh: 语义查询引擎，利用大语言模型对结构化或非结构化数据行进行判断的检索与分析系统。
运行间方差，指相同查询在不同次独立执行或调用时产生结果差异的现象。
用于评估语义查询引擎性能的基准测试集。
可能世界模型，用于预测或模拟多结果可能性的理论模型。
